text: A rotary encoder that gives a unique digital code for every angular position, keeping exact shaft position through power cycles.
A high-pitched noise produced when motor windings vibrate from PWM switching frequencies in the range of human hearing (20 Hz to 20 kHz).
Unfair errors or discrimination in machine learning software, often caused by unbalanced training data, such as failing to detect certain pedestrian groups.
A collision object fixed to a robot link in the planning scene, moving with the tool and checked as part of the robot.
A machine that moves on its own using a built-in mechanism, such as clockwork gears, without sensing or adapting to its surroundings (plural: automata).
Play in a gear train that lets an output move without the input moving, which robot reducers keep to about an arc-minute or less.
A lighting method placing the light behind an object, producing a sharp black silhouette against a bright background for measuring part outlines and dimensions.
An optional UR PolyScope section that runs once before the main loop to put the robot and tools in a known state.
A tree of tasks where each ticked node reports success, failure or running. Nav2 uses one for planning, control and recovery.
An open, two-way digital protocol for absolute encoders that lets a controller read exact shaft positions and exchange configuration or diagnostic data.
A solid-state image sensor where each pixel has its own amplifier and readout circuitry, giving fast frame rates and low power consumption.
A fusion filter that trusts one sensor over short spans and another over long ones, such as a gyroscope and accelerometer for tilt.
An MTC wrapper stage that turns poses from its inner stage, such as grasp poses, into joint configurations by solving inverse kinematics.
A situation where personal, financial, or business interests could bias an engineer's professional judgment. Ethical codes require engineers to disclose such conflicts promptly.
A digital multimeter test done on de-energized, isolated circuits that triggers an audible beep when component resistance drops below a threshold.
The computer that runs a robot's program and decides what to do next, from a microcontroller like an Arduino to an industrial controller.
A programming method where tasks share processor time through non-blocking checks against a clock (such as millis()) instead of delays that freeze the CPU.
A 2D grid of cells, each marked as unknown, free, occupied or inflated, that Nav2 planners search for paths and controllers use to steer.
A technique using a polarizer on the light and an analyzer on the lens at 90 degrees to eliminate specular glare from reflective surfaces.
A ROS package that converts between ROS Image messages and OpenCV NumPy array buffers.
A low-angle lighting method where direct rays reflect away from the lens, while flaws or scratches scatter light into the camera as bright features.
The privacy engineering principle that systems collect, process, and keep only the minimal data strictly necessary for a specified function.
The list in an ament_python package's setup.py telling the build which files, such as launch and YAML files, to copy into the install space.
One independent way a robot moves, each joint adding one. A rigid object in space has six (three for position, three for orientation).
An industrial Ethernet ring topology with an active supervisor transmitting beacon frames, achieving worst-case recovery within 2890 µs on copper with default beacon settings.
An Arduino pin that is HIGH (5 V) or LOW (0 V), used for simple on/off signals such as an LED or bump switch.
The horizontal pixel difference between matching left and right stereo image points. It is inversely proportional to depth, so closer objects have larger disparity.
The two mirror-image postures a two-link arm can use to reach a point, with the elbow on either side of the base-to-target line.
The device mounted on a robot flange that does work, such as a gripper or welding torch. Also called EOAT or end effector.
A mechanical device that can be locked out with a hasp, attachment point, or locking mechanism, excluding push buttons and control circuit devices.
The ERROR section of a RAPID routine that runs when an instruction fails, letting the program retry, skip, return or pass the error on.
A mechanism that lets a power source move a machine forward in small, regular steps. Su Song's 1094 clock tower used one.
A launch system rule that runs actions when something happens to a process, such as shutting everything down when a node exits.
A non-linear Kalman filter that linearizes system functions locally around the current state estimate using first-order Taylor series Jacobian matrices.
A Universal Robots pendant add-on that fetches URScript from the PC ROS driver and runs it so ROS can command the arm.
A paid ABB RobotWare option that lets an external computer stream joint or pose targets to the controller over UDP at a fixed rate.
A camera setup where the camera is mounted on the robot's gripper and moves with it.
A camera setup where the camera is fixed in the cell and watches the work area while the robot moves.
An industrial digital network that replaces point-to-point wiring by connecting sensors, actuators, and controllers over a single shared communication cable.
A system design pattern where a robot stays in one state at a time, switching states when specific sensor events or conditions occur.
A large AI model trained on massive data for many tasks. In robotics, vision-language-action models turn camera images and instructions into robot actions.
A 3D physics simulator that models robots, sensors and environments, connecting to ROS 2 so code can be tested before running on real hardware.
Parts of this site's files that scripts/site_sync.py builds automatically, such as sitemaps, hub rows and navigation bars. They are not edited by hand.
An MTC stage that creates robot states on its own, such as candidate grasp poses, without needing results from neighboring stages.
A formula (DOF = m(N − 1 − J) + Σfᵢ) that finds degrees of freedom from the number of links, joints and joint freedoms.
A circuit of four switches arranged in an 'H' configuration that lets current flow in both directions through a DC motor.
Finding the fixed transform between a camera and a robot gripper or base, usually by solving AX = XB from several robot poses.
A pair of request and reply signals exchanged between a PLC and a robot so each waits for the other before going on.
A ros2_control plugin reading joint states and writing commands to a robot, so controllers above it do not need to know the brand.
A processor mechanism that halts normal program execution when an electrical pin changes state to run an Interrupt Service Routine (ISR).
An error in a mobile robot's estimated orientation. Because later moves drive in the wrong direction, it grows into a large sideways position error.
A system design where a person can understand, check and override what an automated system does.
Weighted sums of pixel intensities across an image contour used to find geometric properties like part area, orientation, and center-of-mass (centroid) coordinates.
A ROS 2 package suite that gives plugin support for publishing and subscribing to compressed image streams.
A condition where an integrator accumulates excessive error while an actuator is saturated, causing severe overshoot and delay when desaturating.
The matrix that converts joint speeds into tool velocity. When its determinant is zero, the robot is at a singularity.
Joseph-Marie Jacquard's 1804 loom attachment using punched cards to control woven patterns, an early machine run by a stored program.
A weighting factor between 0 and 1 that balances trust between a system model and noisy sensor measurements to minimize estimation error covariance.
A programming method where the programmer physically guides the arm through waypoints while the robot records them. It is the main method for cobots.
A sensor that measures distances with laser light. A spinning 2D LiDAR sweeps a beam around the robot to map surroundings in one plane.
A move where the controller drives the TCP along a straight Cartesian line, unlike a joint move (MoveJ) where the tool path is curved.
A rechargeable battery common in mobile robots for high energy density. Battery University gives about 3.6 V nominal per cell.
A world-fixed frame where the robot's pose does not drift but can jump when localization corrects it.
An Arduino function returning milliseconds since board start to time events without blocking. It wraps to zero after about 50 days.
A robot that moves through its environment rather than staying bolted in place, using sensors to map, localize and plan paths.
A ros2_control stand-in that copies commands into its state, so software can be tested with no real robot or physics.
